resources.string: A quiet, always-visible countdown to the next prayer.
Showing the next prayer over other apps. Turn it off in Settings.
AI usage. Pair with your Mac to see your limits here.
Play something to control it here
Media. Play something to control it here.
The island can show what is playing, with a seek bar and a play/pause button, for music, podcasts and video in any app.

To do that Android asks for “Notification access”. Ufuq reads the media session (title, position, play state). If you also turn on “Other apps in the island”, it reads the title and progress of ongoing notifications from the apps you choose. It never reads messages or chats.
Nothing is stored or sent; this never leaves your phone. You can turn it off any time in Android settings.
Allowed. Shows what is playing and lets you seek and pause.
Needs notification access. Reads only media sessions.
%1$s in %2$s, %3$d percent of the time since the previous prayer
%1$s, %2$d percent of the limit used, resets in %3$s
Prayer times are unavailable for this place. Choose another in Settings.
Next prayer in the status bar and on the lock screen. Works with TalkBack. It stays on while the island is on, because Android needs it to keep the island running.
A small island at the camera, over other apps.
Needs permission to display over other apps. Off by default.
Could not get your location. Choose a city instead.
How long before the adhan the island shows a heads-up.
Show the island over other apps
The island is a small black pill at your camera that shows the next prayer, and opens into a card when you tap it.
To draw over other apps, Android asks for the permission “Display over other apps”. Ufuq uses it for the island and nothing else.
Ufuq does not read what is on your screen.
You can turn it off any time in Settings. The Live Update chip shows the same countdown without this permission, and is the best choice with a screen reader.
Rides, deliveries and timers from apps you choose. Off by default.
Only the apps you tick below show here.
Needs notification access to see ongoing notifications.
None yet. An app appears here after it shows a ride, delivery, timer or progress notification.
Show other apps in the island
Ufuq reads the title and progress of ongoing notifications, such as a ride, a delivery, a timer or a download, from the apps you choose.
It does not read messages, chats or any other notification, and ignores apps you have not chosen, media (shown separately) and calls.
Nothing is sent, and the only thing stored is the list of apps you chose.
This uses Android’s notification access, the same permission the media page needs. After you grant it, tick the apps to show in Settings. You can turn it off any time.
Do Not Disturb for a few minutes after each adhan, then back to how it was. Off by default.
Needs Do Not Disturb access. Tap to set it up.
Android is not allowing exact alarms, so silence may start a few minutes late.
Silence while you are within 100 m of a saved mosque, and restore when you leave.
Adding a mosque needs precise location.
Optional. Lets Android tell Ufuq you reached a mosque while the app is closed.
Could not get your location. Try again outdoors.
After each adhan, Ufuq turns on Do Not Disturb for the time you choose, then puts your phone back exactly as it was.
Android keeps this behind a special permission, “Do Not Disturb access”. Ufuq uses it only to switch Do Not Disturb on and off for this.
If you had Do Not Disturb on yourself, Ufuq leaves it alone. If you change it during the silence, Ufuq steps aside. Alarms are never blocked.
Reach a mosque while the app is closed
Saved mosques work by watching for you coming within 100 m. For this to work when Ufuq is not open, Android needs “Allow all the time” location.

Ufuq only compares your position with the places you saved. Your location never leaves your phone. Without it, saved mosques only work while Ufuq is open; the timed silence after each adhan works either way.
Shows when sahur ends (Subuh) and counts down to iftar (Maghrib), with a progress bar. It also turns on by itself during Ramadan.
After you move 25 km or more, Ufuq updates the city and time zone. Coarse location, nothing leaves your phone.
A quiet notice when prayer times move with you.
AI usage. Connecting to your Mac.
AI usage. Your Mac no longer recognises this phone. Pair again to see your limits.
AI usage. Your Mac is not on this network. Ufuq keeps trying.
%1$s. Mac not on this network. Updated %2$s.
Agent task running on your Mac: %1$s
Agent needs input on your Mac: %1$s
See your AI limits and agent status on this phone, over your Wi-Fi.
On your Mac, open Ufuq in the menu bar and choose Pair phone…. A QR code appears. Keep both devices on the same Wi-Fi.
Ufuq uses the camera only on this screen, to read the QR code. Nothing is recorded or saved.
Camera access is off. Allow it in Android settings, or paste the pairing code below.
Camera view. Hold your phone so the QR code on your Mac is inside it.
On the Mac, choose Copy pairing code, then paste it here.
That is not a Ufuq pairing code.
This code is from a different version of Ufuq. Update both apps.
Your AI limits and agent status now show in the island.
Updates are off in development builds. Install the APK from Ufuq\'s GitHub releases to get updates.
A new version of Ufuq is ready to download.
Version %1$s is downloaded. Install it to finish.
Couldn\'t reach GitHub or the download didn\'t verify. Check your connection and try again.
Ufuq checks GitHub once a day for a new version. Turn this off to check only when you ask.
Also offer test versions before they\'re final.
Updates come from github.com/hystericmoon/ufuq. Ufuq sends nothing about you; Android checks that each update is signed with the same key as this app.
